name: foyson

attributes.attribute: stayed creamy but held no nourishment without foyson

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: foyson is a folkloric motive. Every substance holds within it a foyson or toradh, its essence. The foyson of a food means its power to nourish. When fairies stole food they took that power away. The milk may stay in the pail, still creamy in the eye, yet without its foyson it carries no nourishment. Many rituals and verbal charms guarded the foyson of food from the thieves.

okr.objective: foyson is the essence that fairies could strip from food.
key_results: Every substance holds a foyson or toradh, its essence.
